dev.reply:
Yes
As the backend seat, having two drivers active in the same worktree risks clobbered edits, race conditions during test runs, and test pollution. Requiring the facilitator to stop a waiting seat and its background processes by PID before taking over runs protects worktree isolation. Briefing lock-waiting seats to run in the foreground without leaving background watchers is clean, unambiguous, and easy to comply with during red and green phases.
CITE: Stop a waiting seat before its runs are taken over
